channel.title: Market Pressure Map · Indian markets
channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Indian market sectors and the rupee, bonds, inflation and foreign flows.

item.title: Sensex opens about 0.5% higher near 82,033 and Nifty near 25,240 as crude eases; rupee at 94.22
item.description:
Indices recovered Friday's losses in early Monday trade, though realty and metal indices fell about 1%. The rupee opened 3 paise firmer. Wholesale inflation data is due today. Reversing Friday's 0.61% Nifty fall.

Why it matters: Softer oil and continued foreign buying are offsetting rate-hike worries; weak metals reflect poor Chinese data, and the wholesale inflation print is the next test.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1, Rupee +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: days

item.title: Foreign investors bought a net ₹84,291 crore of Indian equities from 2 to 13 November, depository data show
item.description:
That is about $8.9 billion over nine sessions, after October's ₹34,843 crore outflow; debt inflows included ₹7,815 crore via the fully accessible route. 2026 is still a net outflow of about ₹2.56 lakh crore. Ongoing, up from ₹53,739 crore a week ago.

Why it matters: Inflows on this scale underpin equities and the rupee and help fund the wider goods deficit, but can slow as US yields rise.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows +3, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1, Rupee +1, Bond market (G-Secs) +1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: Brent slips 47 cents to $95.37 in Asia as Gulf shipments near pre-war levels and a surplus looms
item.description:
WTI fell 23 cents to $88.33. Traders cited recovering Hormuz flows, the IEA's fourth-quarter surplus forecast and weak Chinese demand, despite new mine claims and an Iranian drone attack on Bahrain. Easing for a third week.

Why it matters: Crude drifting lower despite Gulf attacks suggests supply is winning over fear, which trims India's import bill and fuel-inflation risk.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook +1, Fiscal & trade balance +1, Rupee +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Iran says a supertanker with 2 million barrels sank after mine strikes; India reports a tanker attack
item.description:
Iran's Guards warned ships the strait is closed to unauthorised transit; Indian authorities said a tanker was attacked near Hormuz with crew safe. The US says routes are swept. Escalating from three ships on Saturday.

Why it matters: A sinking, if confirmed, would lift war-risk premiums and tanker rates sharply on India's main crude and LNG route, even while overall flows recover.

Market gauges: Inflation outlook −1, Fiscal & trade balance −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Iran claims six-drone attack on a US base in Bahrain; anti-Houthi forces retreat near Bab el-Mandeb
item.description:
Bahrain issued its first nationwide alerts since September and said the drones were intercepted; the US reported no damage. In Yemen, government forces pulled back near the Red Sea strait. New escalation after Friday's radar strike.

Why it matters: Attacks on Gulf states and a stronger Houthi hold on Bab el-Mandeb threaten both of India's westward energy and trade routes and raise the chance of renewed US strikes.

Market gauges: Equities (Nifty & Sensex) −1, Inflation outlook −1

Confidence: low · horizon: weeks

item.title: A major Japanese container line sends its first ship through the Red Sea and Suez in three years
item.description:
It follows another large carrier's return last week, signalling a gradual resumption by big shipping lines; 122 LNG carriers also used the canal in three months. Easing, though Houthi threats still divert some ships.

Why it matters: Shorter Suez routings cut transit times and freight costs for India's exports to Europe and the US east coast.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +1, Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: months

item.title: China's October factory output slows to 4.8% and retail sales to 0.4%, both below forecasts
item.description:
Output growth was 5.5% in September; retail sales missed the 0.8% forecast. Fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in January–October and building-materials sales dropped 11.2%. New data; slowdown deepening.

Why it matters: Weak Chinese demand depresses metal prices and pushes surplus steel and aluminium abroad, hurting Indian producers, while helping cap oil.

Market gauges: Growth outlook −1, Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: months

item.title: US 10-year yield holds at 5.14% with a December Fed hike fully priced; gold near $3,890 after 4.6% weekly fall
item.description:
The dollar index was steady at 103.42, its highest since April last year; the 2-year yield is 4.87% after a 35 bps weekly jump. The Fed chair speaks today. Ongoing from Friday.

Why it matters: High US yields and a strong dollar keep pressure on the rupee and G-Sec yields and could slow foreign inflows; cheaper gold trims India's import bill.

Market gauges: Rupee −1, Bond market (G-Secs) −1, Foreign investor flows −1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks

item.title: Commerce minister says lower US tariffs than rival nations are 'already agreed' for Indian goods
item.description:
He said Indian goods will get preferential access to the US market. It follows the foreign minister saying the deal is in its final stage. Ongoing; no signing date yet.

Why it matters: Confirmed preferential tariffs would help textiles, engineering and pharma exporters take US market share from Asian rivals.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +1, Foreign investor flows +1, Equities (Nifty & Sensex) +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: months
